version.changelog: 首个版本发布：每日日报对话记录 + 月底一键汇总 + 腾讯文档自动写入

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: daily-report-assistant
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle is a legitimate tool designed to automate daily work reporting to Tencent Docs for a teaching team. It uses the 'mcporter' utility to interact with the Tencent Docs API and includes shell scripts (daily-report.sh, setup.sh) for managing records and authentication tokens. While it contains hardcoded spreadsheet IDs (e.g., DQ1hFandNaE1jZkto in daily-report.sh), the documentation explicitly describes this as a shared team resource for centralized reporting. No evidence of malicious data exfiltration, unauthorized persistence, or harmful prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's stated behavior (write daily records to Tencent 文档) aligns broadly with its code, but there are important mismatches and risky choices (on‑the‑fly npm execution, unclear OAuth/token flow, hard-coded file IDs) that the installer should verify before trusting it with credentials or installing widely.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim to read/write Tencent 文档 and produce monthly summaries — the scripts do exactly that (they read/write a Tencent Docs 'file_id' and sheet ids). No unrelated cloud providers or system credentials are requested. However the skill embeds fixed file_id and sheet IDs in multiple scripts, which means it will attempt to read/write a specific remote document by default; confirm those IDs point to your team's doc and not some third party.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells users to click an authorization link and tell the skill their name. The included shell scripts, however, require additional manual setup steps (running scripts/setup.sh, invoking setup.sh auth <token>, and having npx/node available). The SKILL.md does not document the need for Node/npm, mcporter, or manual token entry, creating a gap between the user-facing instructions and what the code actually requires. The code reads/writes local memory files under ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory and will call out to Tencent Docs API endpoints — all consistent with purpose but the flow to obtain and set the API token is ambiguous in the user-facing instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec, but the scripts repeatedly call `npx -y mcporter ...` which downloads and executes an npm package at runtime. This means arbitrary code from the npm registry will be pulled and executed on first use (network and npm required). That behavior is expected for the chosen mcporter approach but increases risk compared to an instruction-only skill that never auto-fetches packages. The repository itself does not vendor mcporter; calls rely on network/npm.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, but it implicitly requires: Node/npm (npx), python3, network access, and that the operator obtain a Tencent Docs authorization token and set it via `setup.sh auth <token>` which stores the token into mcporter config (`npx mcporter config add ... --header 'Authorization=<token>' --scope home`). The token is necessary and appropriate for the stated purpose, but the skill will store it in mcporter's configuration (user home scope) rather than in a single skill file — users should understand where their token is stored. No other credentials are requested, which is proportionate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true'. It writes a local user-config file under the workspace memory and writes mcporter config (token) in the user's home scope. That is normal for a connector that needs persistent credentials, but note the token is stored outside the skill folder (mcporter config), so revoking/removing access requires handling mcporter configs as well as the Tencent Docs authorization in your account. The skill does not modify other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing/using this skill, verify these points: 1) Source and ownership — the package has no homepage and unknown source; confirm you trust the maintainer. 2) Tokens and OAuth — you will need to authorize Tencent 文档 and set a token (scripts expect you to run setup.sh auth <token>); ask the publisher to explain the exact OAuth flow if unclear. 3) Where data goes — the scripts use hard-coded file_id and sheet IDs; confirm those IDs point to your organization's documents (or plan to change them) to avoid writing to someone else's document. 4) Runtime behavior — the scripts call `npx -y mcporter` which will pull and run code from npm on first use; ensure you are comfortable with that and have Node/npm available. 5) Storage & revocation — the token is stored via mcporter in your home config (not just the skill folder); decide how to revoke it when needed. If you are not comfortable with these gaps, request a version that documents the token/OAuth flow and avoids on‑the‑fly npm execution (or run the skill in an isolated/sandboxed environment first).
